extraction.name: Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities
extraction.description: VQAonline is the first Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums, it contains authentic context that clarifies the question, an answer the individual asking the question validated as acceptable, answers that are considerably longer (mean of 173 words), and user-chosen topics for each visual question from 105 diverse topics.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari
extraction.publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Microsoft, University of Colorado Boulder
extraction.citeAs: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari. Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.15562, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. Data was collected from August 2010 to November 2022, adhering to the cc-by-sa 4.0 data license. Examples containing a natural language question (post 'title'), a natural language context ('body' text entry field supporting inline images), an image (URL link), and at least one answer were collected. The individual who posted the visual question could mark an answer as 'accepted', and only examples with an accepted answer were used.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web Scraping, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly-available data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange archive, spanning from August 2010 to November 2022.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two filtering steps were conducted to obtain the final dataset of 64,696 VQAs. First, visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer (based on user up-votes/down-votes) were removed. Second, visual questions with multiple images (e.g., GIF) or with visual answers were excluded. Additionally, visual questions without an accepted answer were removed, and examples for which the image could not be downloaded were excluded. All images were converted to PNG format for data format consistency.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset's answers are user-generated and validated by the individual asking the question on Stack Exchange, who marked an answer as 'accepted'. User-chosen topics for each visual question from 105 diverse topics are also part of the dataset. Additionally, a subset of 105 visual questions had their user intent annotated by three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Annotators were shown the visual question, context, and answer, and asked to categorize the primary user intention into one of eight categories (advice, evidence, identification, instruction, opinion, reason, verification, and other) after one-on-one Zoom training and a qualifying test.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk, home-grown web-based interface
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intent annotations, two independent workers (A and B) annotated each VQA instance. Disagreements were resolved by a third worker (C) who broke the tie. Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen’s kappa agreement improved from 45.24% to 84.69% over four rounds of analysis.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For user intent annotation: Three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk, located in the United States, with over 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) completed and over a 95% approval rating. For model evaluation: Ten human annotators, each a domain expert in one of ten specific topics (Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, Artificial Intelligence) with at least a Master’s degree in a related field, located in the United States.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improved models designed for VQAonline can benefit various real-world applications, including other community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, and visual search and browsing.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits a high prevalence of screenshots (79-84%) and infographics (17-33%), reflecting Stack Exchange users’ tendency to ask questions about the digital realm and data analysis. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more data from countries like the US, India, and Europe, and less from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas due to VQAs being posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and the internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more data from countries like the US, India, and Europe, and less from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The dataset is intended for developing and evaluating Visual Question Answering (VQA) models, particularly those designed for authentic use cases with lengthy textual answers and contextual information.
